themes.description: Semantic color tokens per theme, from tokens/tokens.json (CSS custom properties --ply-color-*).

dataviz.validation: Adjacent pairs checked for color vision deficiency: worst delta E 13.6 light and 13.6 dark; normal vision 18.0 light and 16.7 dark. Scatter and small multiples use the first three slots only.

components.name: Exhibit
components.description: The emblem: a Vietoris-Rips complex in a black panel, with a wall-label caption underneath.
components.css: .ds-exhibit { margin: 0; max-width: 35rem; font-family: "Libre Franklin", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-panel { aspect-ratio: 100 / 56; background: #141414; } .ds-panel svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; } .ds-tri { fill: #E9A81C; fill-opacity: 0.5; } .ds-edge { stroke: #F6F7F6; stroke-opacity: 0.7; stroke-width: 0.28; } .ds-pt { fill: #F6F7F6; transition: fill 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-pt:hover { fill: #D9412B; } .ds-exhibit figcaption { margin-top: 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.45; color: #4A4A47; } .ds-exhibit figcaption b { color: #141414; }

components.name: Atlas
components.description: A CV as a 1-complex on the sphere: an orthographic globe in a black panel, drawn like the complex, with chalk points and great-circle route, mustard countries that hold a place, the tomato ball and dashed reach on the current place, and a wall-label caption that names the current entry, or counts places and moves.
components.css: .ds-atlas { margin: 0; max-width: 35rem; font-family: "Libre Franklin", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-atlas-map { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 10 / 7; background: #141414; } .ds-atlas-map svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; } .ds-sea { fill: #F6F7F6; fill-opacity: 0.05; stroke: #F6F7F6; stroke-opacity: 0.3; stroke-width: 0.4; } .ds-grid { fill: none; stroke: #F6F7F6; stroke-opacity: 0.1; stroke-width: 0.25; } .ds-land { fill: #F6F7F6; fill-opacity: 0.13; stroke: #F6F7F6; stroke-opacity: 0.6; stroke-width: 0.25; } .ds-visited { fill: #E9A81C; fill-opacity: 0.5; } .ds-route { fill: none; stroke: #F6F7F6; stroke-opacity: 0.8; stroke-width: 0.4; } .ds-pt { fill: #F6F7F6; stroke: #141414; stroke-width: 0.5; transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; } .ds-pt:hover { transform: scale(1.3); } .ds-reach { fill: none; stroke: #D9412B; stroke-width: 0.5; stroke-dasharray: 1.2 0.9; } .ds-here { fill: #D9412B; stroke: #141414; stroke-width: 0.5; } .ds-atlas-tag { position: absolute; left: 51%; top: 64%; padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem; background: #F6F7F6; color: #141414; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-atlas figcaption { margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.45; color: #4A4A47; } .ds-atlas figcaption b { color: #141414; }

narrative.overview:
Polytope is set as a hands-on mathematics exhibition, after the 1961 exhibition by Charles and Ray Eames. The page is a white gallery. Content hangs on it in exhibit-black panels, regions are divided by heavy 3px rules, titles are cut in wood type, and every chapter opens with a working model the reader can run. The models are real: the emblem is a Vietoris-Rips complex whose radius the reader drags, and a Galton board drops balls live and settles into a bell curve.

Color is scarce and each color has one job. Tomato marks the current location and the moving part. Mustard marks notes and always carries black text. Teal marks links and links are always underlined. Everything else is black, white, and gallery gray. Density is calm: a 36rem reading column, wide gutters, generous space between sections, with tables and code held to the same edge as the prose.

Corners are square. The only round things are things that are round in the world: balls, points, radio buttons, status dots. Depth comes from black panels against white and from heavy rules; shadows appear only under layers that float above the page. Dark mode is the exhibition after hours: the ground goes near black and panels sit one step lighter than the ground.
keyCharacteristics: White gallery ground, exhibit-black panels, 3px black rules between regions.
Ultra wood-type titles in sentence case ending in a tomato full stop.
Tomato for where you are and what moves; mustard for notes; teal for links.
Square corners everywhere except balls and points.
A working model in a black panel with a wall-label caption opens every chapter.
A Vietoris-Rips complex is the emblem: it opens the home page and draws the favicon.
One signature moment of motion per page; reduced motion shows the end state.

rules.name: The One Moving Part Rule
rules.body: Tomato marks the current location and the thing that moves, and the small marks that lead the eye to them: the full stop, list markers, reference numbers. It never fills a panel or colors a paragraph.

rules.name: The Black Text on Mustard Rule
rules.body: Mustard always carries exhibit-black text, in both themes, including links inside notes.

rules.name: The Underlined Link Rule
rules.body: Links are teal and always underlined. Color alone never marks a link.

rules.name: The Mark and Word Rule
rules.body: Status and note kind are carried by a shape and a word: ball for note, triangle for warning, check for success, cross for danger. Color never carries status alone.

rules.name: The Wood Type Rule
rules.body: Ultra is for titles only, at 24px and up, in sentence case. Everything that gets read is Libre Franklin.

rules.name: The Full Stop Rule
rules.body: Mast titles and the wordmark end in a tomato full stop that never wraps away from its word.

rules.name: The Wall and Panel Rule
rules.body: Depth is a black panel on a white wall. Shadows belong only to layers that float and go away.

rules.name: The Only Round Things Rule
rules.body: If it is not a ball or a point, its corners are square.

dos: Do open every chapter landing with a working model in a black panel, captioned underneath like a wall label.
Do keep text, tables, and code in one column on the same 36rem edge, with notes and margin figures beside it; never let a block straddle the edge between text and margin.
Do end mast titles in a tomato full stop and size them to the longest word.
Do use ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) for things that arrive and the gravity curve (`cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 1, 0.45)`) for things that fall.
Do give each page one signature moment of motion and show the end state under reduced motion.
Do assign chart colors in the fixed slot order and limit scatter plots and small multiples to the first three.
Do check every new color pair with the contrast script in both themes (WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for marks, rings, and borders).
Do write plain, specific copy with no dashes as punctuation and no sales words.
donts: Don't use tomato for anything other than the current location, a moving part, or the small marks that lead to them.
Don't put white or colored text on mustard.
Don't show a link without its underline.
Don't set Ultra below 24px, in all caps, or for running text.
Don't round a corner unless the shape is a ball or a point.
Don't put shadows on panels, buttons, cards, or anything that stays on the page.
Don't let color carry status by itself; pair it with a shape and a word.
Don't cycle chart colors past the eighth slot or reorder them.
